final:
All 53 requested tests pass, including the new regression test.

**What was wrong.** Attachments inherit permissions from the model they are attached to. The API enforced this for create, update, and delete, but not for reading. Any authenticated user could list every attachment in the system via the attachment list endpoint, or fetch any attachment by ID, regardless of whether they could view the linked model. That exposes file URLs and comments for purchase orders, sales orders, companies, and so on to users who have no role on those models.

**What I changed** in `src/backend/InvenTree/common/api.py`:

- The attachment list view now overrides `filter_queryset` and excludes every model type for which the user lacks the view role. Superusers see everything. Unknown or stale model types are hidden rather than exposed.
- The attachment detail view now checks the view permission on retrieve and returns 403 when it fails. I kept this as an explicit check rather than queryset filtering so the existing 403 responses on unauthorised update and delete are unchanged.

**Test added** in `src/backend/InvenTree/common/test_api.py`: a user with no roles sees an empty list and gets 403 on detail; granting only the part view role exposes the part attachment but not the company one, even when filtering explicitly by model type; a superuser sees both.

The parameter list endpoint has the same read gap, but I left it alone since the request was for a single change.

CHOICE: I made attachment list and detail reads enforce the linked model's view permission, because unauthenticated-by-role users could previously read every attachment in the system while writes were already protected.
